concept: Region and Cloud Provider Price Differentials for Atlas
summary: Atlas prices differ by cloud provider (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) and by region: the Atlas docs state that the provider and region choice affects the cost of a cluster, and the pricing page quotes dedicated-tier base prices for one reference region per provider (AWS us-east-1, Azure eastus2, Google Cloud us-central1) while only Online Archive lists rates region by region. Backup storage, data transfer (cheapest within a region, dearest across providers or to the Internet) and multi-region nodes also vary by provider and region. The pack holds 85 source-anchored units from 5 sources (4 hosts) across 9 facets, mostly measures and facts.

facts.text: Atlas docs state that the choice of cloud provider and region affects cluster cost. For multi-region clusters, cost depends on the number and location of additional regions; the creation UI shows the tier cost for the Preferred Region only, and the Cluster Overview shows the true total.
The cost for Cloud Backups is calculated per GB per month. Rates vary between cloud providers and between regions within a given cloud provider.
_[1] Based on Virginia (eastus2) region._

Atlas tabulates data transfer costs daily. Pricing varies by cloud provider and by the region of the source and destination nodes. This page describes sources of data transfer costs, pricing by provider, and strategies to reduce costs.

Atlas supports deploying clusters onto Amazon Web Services, the Google Cloud Platform, and Microsoft Azure. The choice of cloud service provider and region or regions for the Atlas project affects the cost of running a Atlas cluster.

- **Cluster tier and type:** The selected tier is the foundational cost driver. Higher tiers provide more dedicated resources and capabilities. - **Cloud provider and region:** Costs vary slightly across AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure, and between different geographic regions. - **Data storage:** Includes the size of your data and indexes. - **Data transfer (networking):** Charges mainly apply to data moving out of your Atlas cluster (egress) or between different regions/cloud providers. Inbound data transfers are typically free. Free and Flex tiers are not charged for outgoing data. -

Multi-region cluster costs depend on the number of and location of additional regions selected. When creating a cluster, Atlas displays the cluster tier cost based on only the Preferred Region of the cluster. You can see the total cost of running the cluster in the Cluster Overview.

Depending on the choice of cloud service provider, Atlas provides customization options for cluster storage capacity and the speed of that storage. If you add capacity or speed, you incur additional costs on top of the base cost. For multi-region clusters, the per-cluster cost, including any selected customizations, is relative to the Preferred Region. The Cluster Overview box shows your overall charges.
Cross region data transfer when you copy your backups to another region.

Incrementality is determined by your cluster's cloud service provider. To compute the cost for Cloud Backups, Atlas obtains the raw metric data from the cloud providers and calculates the total size of all snapshots based on the region where it stores the snapshot and the amount of storage used per month.

If Atlas must retain more than one snapshot, Atlas stores the new snapshot in the same region as the cluster's current backup node. Atlas continues using that backup node for snapshots and snapshot storage.

If you have fast disk pre-warming enabled for an M40+ cluster hosted on AWS, Atlas may temporarily provision a higher performance AWS storage volume when replacing a node or provisioning an additional node. This reduces how long the Cloud-based initial sync takes.

Atlas adds the cost of the higher performance disk to your regular storage costs in your monthly Atlas bill. You may notice a higher storage cost than expected in your Atlas bill in months where Atlas provisions or replaces a node on an M40+ AWS cluster.

When you switch your cluster from Gen1 to Gen2, your cluster may have a higher IOPS rate than the baseline included with your storage capacity. After switching to Gen2, we recommend you adjust your storage capacity and IOPS rate independently to fit your workload and optimize your costs. To learn more, see Change a Cluster's Generation.

Atlas measures storage speed as maximum IOPS. Each Atlas cluster tier offers a default storage speed that is included in the cluster's per-hour cost. The choice of cloud service provider and cluster affects the available storage speed customization options and the cost of selecting a custom storage speed.

Gen2 Dedicated clusters have a baseline minimum IOPS based on the cluster's disk storage. The charges from Atlas for Gen2 cluster storage capacity include the baseline minimum IOPS for that disk size. On top of the baseline minimum IOPS, you can provision Extended Standard IOPS for Gen2 Dedicated clusters. Atlas charges separately for Extended Standard IOPS you provision beyond the baseline IOPS. To learn more about your cluster's baseline minimum IOPS rate, see Extended Standard IOPS.

All clusters use SSD persistent disks with fixed maximum IOPS based on the cluster storage capacity. The maximum IOPS increases as storage capacity increases. The cost of the increased maximum IOPS is included in the cost of the increased storage capacity. To learn more about the Google Cloud persistent disks, see Persistent Disks.
Modify the backup policy to reduce the number of snapshots automatically copied to additional regions

- Avoid queries that re-read client data or re-write existing cluster data. - Use query projections to only retrieve necessary fields. - Deploy applications in the same cloud region as the Atlas cluster. - Enable network compression in client drivers to reduce data volume.
facts.note: Atlas FAQ: ways to cut data transfer

facts.text: Source write queries from your Highest Priority Region whenever possible. For more information on region priorities, see Electable Nodes for High Availability.
Ensure that queries originate from the same cloud region and provider as your cluster whenever possible.
Ensure read queries use the preference "nearest."

In those reference regions, M30 (8 GB RAM, 2 vCPU) lists at $0.54/hr on AWS, $0.51/hr on Azure and $0.44/hr on GCP; M50 lists at $2.00, $1.95 and $1.66/hr; M10 is $0.08/hr on all three. GCP is the cheapest at M30 and above, roughly 18% below AWS at M30.

Data transfer costs for downloading the snapshot over the public Internet or for downloading the snapshot over private endpoints for Atlas clusters on AWS or Azure with private endpoints. These costs vary by cloud provider and region. To learn more, see Private Endpoint Billing.
facts.note: Restore downloads; AWS and Azure private endpoints

facts.text: Atlas states most customers spend under 10% of budget on data transfer; mitigations are co-locating apps in the cluster's region and provider and using nearest read preference for unavoidable cross-region reads.

Real-world bills tend to surprise teams who only scoped the hourly instance rate. Consider a common SaaS setup: one M10 cluster for development and staging (~$57/month) and one M30 for production (~$190/month), both on AWS us-east-1. Add backup storage at roughly $0.14/GB for 40 GB ($5.60/month) plus modest cross-region data transfer, and you’re already at $260–$280/month before any support plans or additional Atlas features. Scale to an M50 production cluster with a global multi-region deployment and Atlas Search enabled, and $1,000+/month is realistic.

For example, if you copy all of your backups to one additional region, you pay for approximately twice the storage: an amount for your standard backup, and approximately the same amount for your copies stored in the other region (storage costs vary by region).

facts.text: Atlas charges $0.125 per GB of data exported to the AWS S3 bucket, Azure Blob Storage Container, or Google Cloud Storage bucket in addition to the data transfer cost incurred from the cloud service itself. Atlas compresses the data before exporting. To estimate the amount of data being exported, add up the dataSize of each database in your cluster. This total should correspond to the uncompressed size of your export, which would be the maximum cost incurred from Atlas for the data export operation.

facts.note: Stream Processing tiers, AWS; cost per hour is a range

facts.text: Queries from on-premises environments into Atlas, across cloud providers, or between continents on the same cloud provider incur the greatest data transfer costs.
Backups – Pricing starts at $0.14 per GB per month, depending on the size of your datafiles on the disk.
Customers with existing deployments in legacy regions can continue to access their data, but new archives cannot be created in these regions.

Tier shapes are not identical across providers: M10 is 2 vCPU/2 GB on AWS, 1 vCPU/2 GB on Azure and 0.5 vCPU/1.7 GB on GCP at the same $0.08/hr list price, and the GCP M20 has 3.75 GB RAM vs 4 GB elsewhere. Price per hour alone is not like-for-like.
M30+ Dedicated clusters on AWS or Google Cloud are available in cluster generations Gen1 or Gen2. Gen1 clusters have IOPS, storage, and costs that differ from Gen2 clusters of the same cluster class.

For multi-region deployments, costs are higher than single-region clusters, as they require multiple nodes across regions and incur additional replication and data transfer charges, rather than following a fixed starting price.
Multi-region clusters — These carry a premium over single-region equivalents even at identical instance sizes

A third-party guide says AWS us-east-1 is typically among the lowest-cost regions and quotes $0.01/GB same-region and $0.02/GB cross-region transfer plus $0.09/GB Internet egress; these are generic AWS-style figures, not Atlas-published rates.

Pricing varies by cloud provider and region (with AWS us-east-1 typically among the lowest-cost options), and does not include additional charges such as backups, data transfer, or optional Atlas features.

Export Logs to External Services routes through the Atlas control plane in AWS us-east-1 regardless of cluster region or provider, so clusters elsewhere pay cross-region or inter-cloud transfer on top of Internet egress.

The public Atlas pricing page quotes dedicated-tier base prices for a single reference region per provider: AWS N. Virginia (us-east-1), Azure Virginia (eastus2), GCP Iowa (us-central1). Prices include default storage and change if storage is customized.

Atlas data-transfer pricing varies by cloud provider and by the region of source and destination nodes. Transfers rank from cheapest to costliest: same region/zone, cross-region within a provider, then out to the Internet or another provider. Inbound data is free; multi-region clusters can have higher transfer costs.

Cloud Backup storage is billed per GB per month with rates that vary between providers and between regions within a provider (docs example: $0.14/GB-month for an AWS region); continuous-backup snapshot/oplog rates are likewise tabulated by provider and region.

Export Logs to External Services routes log traffic through the Atlas control plane in AWS us-east-1, regardless of your cluster's region or cloud provider. If your cluster is not in AWS us-east-1, you incur cross-region or inter-cloud data transfer charges in addition to Internet egress costs.
Push Logs to AWS S3 exports logs directly from the data node to an S3 bucket in the cluster's region. Standard Internet egress costs apply.

M40, M50, M60, M80, M200, and M400 cluster tiers support Non-Volatile Memory Express Solid State Drives (NVMe SSDs) storage for AWS. These are dedicated clusters and automatically scale up to the next higher tier once 90% of available storage is used. These clusters are available in the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific regions. You can’t pause an NVMe cluster.
Multi-region clusters might have higher data transfer costs depending on the number and location of additional regions, as well as the number of clusters deployed to each region.
M60, M80, M200, M300, M400, and M600 dedicated clusters support NVMe on Microsoft Azure. See the availability zones here and here. You won’t be able to pause an NVMe cluster.

facts.text: MongoDB hosts and operates the free Atlas Live Migration Service to help you migrate existing MongoDB databases to MongoDB Atlas. MongoDB doesn't charge for any incoming data transfers to an Atlas cluster. Learn more about migrating to Atlas.
AWS instance type, AWS region, consumption, and other factors, like data transfer and backup policy, will also affect your MongoDB spend on AWS.
Select your cloud provider to view the applicable data transfer costs.
